answer: An island registry grants weight to a stake thread clearing a cipher threshold. An applicant locks 90 credits into one island thread, recorded in a glacier ledger under a cipher that cannot move islands. Below 90, weight is zero, so splitting capital into dust identities earns nothing. The k-th fake must lock 90, so cost grows as 90k: 1,000 fakes lock 90,000 credits. Auditors replay the glacier ledger and island threads, freezing pooled stakes. A stake-pooling ring fails because pooled stake counts as one thread, not 1,000 identities.
